test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A concave mirror having focal length of magnitude 20 cm forms a real image at a distance of 60 cm from it. The object distance (in cm) is:
solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Concave Mirror Formula:**

__
 
• The relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a concave mirror is given by the mirror formula:
 
• **Mirror Formula:** (1)/(f) = (1)/(v) + (1)/(u) 
 
• Here, **f** is the focal length (cm), **v** is the image distance (cm), and **u** is the object distance (cm).
 
• The focal length (f) of a concave mirror is negative, and the image distance (v) for a real image is also negative.
 
• **Real Image:** An image formed where the light rays converge. It is inverted and can be projected onto a screen.
 
• **SI Unit:** The SI unit of focal length is meter (m), but in this context, we use centimeters (cm).
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for focal length is [L].

 

**Calculation:**__

Given,

Focal length, f = -20 cm

Image distance, v = -60 cm

Using mirror formula,

(1)/(f) = (1)/(v) + (1)/(u)

⇒ (1)/(-20) = (1)/(-60) + (1)/(u)

⇒ (1)/(u) = (1)/(-20) - (1)/(-60)

⇒ (1)/(u) = (-3 + 1)/(60)

⇒ (1)/(u) = (-2)/(60)

⇒ (1)/(u) = -(1)/(30)

⇒ u = -30 cm

**∴ The object distance is -30 cm.**
